data.name: Vrinda
data.gender_notes: Vrinda is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘vrindam’, meaning a wreath or a garland. The name ‘Vrinda’ is derived from the ancient Indian mythology, where Vrinda is known as the tree of love and devotion. This name symbolizes boundless love, loyalty, and the circularity of life, making it an ideal choice for a baby girl. The name Vrinda carries the meaning “boundless, circular, wreath, garland” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Vrinda usually hope their child will grow to embody boundless, circular, wreath, garland and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and spirituality, symbolizing the love and devotion of the god Krishna for his beloved Radha. Vrinda is also the name of a tree in Hindu mythology, which is believed to be a symbol of eternal love and devotion. It is said that those named Vrinda are blessed with the ability to give and receive love unconditionally and to maintain long-lasting relationships.
data.etymology: Vrinda belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “boundless, circular, wreath, garland.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vrinda total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.
